Independent integer grid replay: for q=p/M compare ordered totals as M(s+a-C)_+ + (p min(C,s+a)+M(b-C))_+; take C=2..11, s=1..C-1, 2<=A<=2C, 1<=B<A, and p=1..22 with M=23. All 159720 comparisons and all 1980 extra straddling tests at (p,M)=(s,s+B) agree exactly.
correctness.rationale: The absolutely continuous solution of the loss equation multiplies post-first storage by q=exp(-K). Summing the overflows gives the displayed positive-part identity. If neither first pulse overflows, the small-first sequence has the larger second overflow argument by (1-q)(A-B), so the difference is nonpositive. If both first pulses saturate, they have the same post-first storage and their first-runoff difference A-B cannot be exceeded by the opposite second-runoff difference, by the 1-Lipschitz positive part. These cases include s+A=C and s+B=C respectively. In the strict straddling case put y=s+B and q0=s/y. The larger-first second overflow becomes active only above (C-B)/C, strictly above q0 because y<C. Until that activation the sign is the sign of s-qy: the larger-first first overflow is positive, and the small-first second positive part exceeds, equals, or falls short of that positive value precisely as qy exceeds, equals, or falls short of s. Above activation the difference simplifies to (1-q)(y-C)<0. This gives one zero in q and the stated strict signs in K, with arbitrary nonnegative integrable proportional-loss profiles.
residual_risks: The weak-sign regimes can tie. Results concern two instantaneous impulses in a single proportional-loss, capped store, not field-scale runoff or any arbitrary inter-event law.

originality.rationale: The distinct indexed two-roof result 56bb6286d54f already gives the decisive general single-roof straddling identity as part of its proof. The change from a starting-saturation sweep to a loss-dose sweep solves that same identity for another variable. Even enforcing the earlier record's pre-drying restriction, every critical point and its two-sided neighborhood are covered, and the excluded high-loss range is trivially of one sign. The central novelty asserted for the frozen threshold therefore is not established as a distinct result. This is a coverage comparison of two original statements, not a claim that their same-day indexing proves chronological priority or that the frozen theorem is false.
residual_risks: Same-day timestamps do not establish chronological priority. The finding fails because its distinct mathematical contribution is not established versus inspected coverage, not because a paper was inaccessible.

value.rationale: There is practical interpretive value in reporting the threshold as an integrated loss dose, but the scientific addition here is only solving the existing exact switch identity for q, converting variables to K, and extending the weak signs to unconstrained transient starts by immediate positive-part bounds. The removed preparatory interval does not create a new threshold regime or a new switching phenomenon, since every threshold is already attainable under the earlier restriction. No separate valuable new mathematical remainder is established, so no repair is submitted.
residual_risks: This assessment concerns distinct scientific contribution; it does not deny the usefulness or correctness of the formula as a restatement for single-store modeling.
